title: Ultra-Processed Foods May Dull Your Focus
hook: In 2,100 adults, eating more ultra-processed food tracked with poorer attention and slower thinking — even among people whose diets were otherwise healthy.
key_points: Study of more than 2,100 adults linked higher ultra-processed food intake to poorer attention and slower mental processing.
The pattern held even among people with otherwise healthy diets.
Higher consumption was also tied to more dementia risk factors.
It's an association — but it adds a possible cognitive cost to a food category already linked to other harms.
content_html: Ultra-processed foods are already linked to heart disease, diabetes, and weight gain. A study of more than 2,100 adults adds a subtler concern: people who ate more of them had poorer attention and slower mental processing — and that held even among those whose diets were otherwise healthy.
extra_html: Higher ultra-processed intake was also associated with more dementia risk factors, raising the possibility of a hidden cognitive cost. As an observational study, it shows a link rather than proof that these foods directly dull thinking. Still, it's one more reason the "mostly whole foods" advice keeps holding up. Reported by ScienceDaily.

flashcards.explanation_html: Across 2,100 adults, higher ultra-processed intake tracked with weaker attention and slower mental processing, plus more dementia risk factors.

flashcards.prompt: Why is the 'even among healthy eaters' detail notable?
flashcards.back_html: It suggests ultra-processed foods were tied to weaker attention and processing regardless of overall diet quality — the link wasn't just a stand-in for eating badly overall.

flashcards.prompt: What kind of evidence is this, and what does that mean?
flashcards.back_html: It's observational — a link across 2,100 adults, not proof that ultra-processed foods directly impair thinking.
